footer.disclaimer: OpenCPAP is an informational tool, not a medical device. It does not diagnose or recommend therapy changes. Talk to your clinician about your data.
footer.privacy: All processing happens in your browser. Nothing is uploaded.

import.title: Import CPAP data
import.privacy: The files are read and decoded locally by your browser. They are never uploaded.
import.folderHint: Your browser will ask for permission to read the folder. Only reading is requested.
import.errorUnsupported: No supported CPAP data was found. Select the card's root folder: it contains P-SERIES for a Philips DreamStation 2, or DATALOG and STR.edf for a ResMed AirSense/AirCurve.
import.errorDnd: Drop a folder or a ZIP file.
import.demoBody: Explore the app with synthetic example data.
import.step1: Remove the card from your CPAP and put it in your computer, or copy its contents to a folder.
import.step2: Pick the card's root folder: it contains P-SERIES for a Philips DreamStation 2, or DATALOG and STR.edf for a ResMed AirSense/AirCurve. You can also drop it here or use a ZIP.
import.step3: Sessions are decoded on this device and stored in your browser.

dashboard.demoBanner: You are viewing synthetic demo data.
dashboard.complianceDetail: {{ok}} of {{total}} nights with at least 4 h
dashboard.tableHint: Select a night to see details.
dashboard.subtitle: {{count}} nights stored · latest {{date}}

explain.ahi: Apnea–Hypopnea Index: apneas and hypopneas per hour of use. Many guidelines treat under 5 per hour as well controlled, but what is right for you is a decision for your clinician.
explain.usage: Hours with the mask on. Many insurers and clinics look for at least 4 hours on at least 70 % of nights.
explain.leak: Air leak, in litres per minute. Philips devices report total leak, which includes the deliberate leak of the mask vents, so a steady non-zero value is normal. ResMed devices report unintentional leak, with the vent flow already subtracted, so their values are lower and start near zero. Sustained high peaks may mean a poor mask seal. The two kinds should not be compared with each other.
explain.pressure: Therapy pressure in cmH₂O set on the device or chosen automatically.
explain.compliance: Share of nights with at least 4 hours of use over the last 30 nights.
explain.flow: Breathing flow measured by the device (positive: breathing in). Scaling is approximate.
explain.rera: Respiratory Effort Related Arousals: breathing effort events that disturb sleep without being a full apnea or hypopnea. They are not part of the AHI.
explain.rate: Breaths per minute, taken from the time between breaths in the flow signal. At 5 samples per second it is quantised in steps of about one breath per minute at higher rates.
explain.regularity: How much the length of one breath differs from the next (coefficient of variation). Lower means a steadier rhythm; sleep stage, position and arousals all change it.
explain.flat: Share of breaths whose inspiratory flow is flat-topped rather than rounded, a sign the airway may be partly narrowed. Experimental: while developing it, flat-topped breaths were about 2.7 times more common in the minute before events the device itself flagged as flow limitation.
explain.periodic: Share of the night with a sustained, regular waxing and waning of breath size (periods of 20 to 120 s lasting several minutes), as in periodic breathing. Brief episodes, like the few minutes the device itself sometimes reports, are not detected: its own periodic-breathing events remain the reference.
explain.ie: How much longer expiration lasts than inspiration (typically 1.2 to 2).
explain.odi: Oxygen desaturation index: how many times per hour SpO₂ fell by at least 3 (or 4) points below its recent level for 10 s to 3 min. It depends on the sensor and its averaging; compare it with your own earlier nights.
explain.t90: Share of the valid recording with SpO₂ under 90 %.
explain.spo2: Blood oxygen saturation measured by your oximeter.

night.noWaveform: This night has no detailed flow data on the card; only summary statistics are shown.
night.zoomHint: Drag on a chart to zoom, double-click to reset.
night.altHypopnea: Includes hypopneas that the device itself does not count.
night.noEvents: No events were recorded this night.
night.settingsHint: As reported by the device for this night

settings.title: Settings
settings.deleteAllConfirm: Delete all stored CPAP data, notes and equipment from this browser? This cannot be undone.
settings.privacyBody: OpenCPAP runs entirely in your browser. Imported data is stored in this browser only (IndexedDB) and is never sent anywhere.
settings.backupBody: Save your therapy data, notes and equipment to a file, or restore them from one. Backups are compressed and stay on your device.
settings.includeWaveforms: Include detailed flow data (much larger file; it can be re-imported from the card)
settings.importDone: Restored {{sessions}} sessions, {{journal}} notes and {{equipment}} equipment items.
settings.importSkipped: {{count}} entries in the file were not valid and were skipped.
settings.persistBody: Ask the browser not to clear this data when the device is low on space.
settings.persistNo: The browser may clear this data if space runs low. A backup is the safest copy.
settings.persistDenied: The browser did not grant it. Installing the app often helps.
settings.persistUnsupported: This browser does not support persistent storage.
settings.backupWarning: Backups are not encrypted: keep the file somewhere private.

hero.trendUsage: Hours of use over the last 30 nights

journal.title: Notes
journal.notePlaceholder: How did you sleep? Anything unusual: illness, alcohol, a new mask…
journal.tagPlaceholder: Add a tag and press Enter
journal.private: Notes stay in this browser. They are included in backups and, only if you choose, in the report.

findings.title: Summary of the night
findings.disclaimer: Generated from your numbers with fixed rules. It is not a diagnosis or advice; talk to your clinician about your data.

finding.usageOk: You used the device for {{time}}, above the common 4 h target.
finding.usageShort: You used the device for {{time}}, under the common 4 h target.
finding.usageVeryShort: The device was used for only {{time}} this night.
finding.ahiLow: Your AHI was {{ahi}} events per hour, under 5.
finding.ahiMid: Your AHI was {{ahi}} events per hour, between 5 and 15.
finding.ahiHigh: Your AHI was {{ahi}} events per hour, 15 or more.
finding.ahiAboveUsual: That is higher than your usual {{usual}}.
finding.ahiBelowUsual: That is lower than your usual {{usual}}.
finding.leakHigh: Leak (95 %) was {{leak}} L/min, above your usual {{usual}} L/min.
finding.largeLeak: The device reported large leaks for about {{minutes}} min.
finding.maskOff_one: The mask was taken off {{count}} time (about {{minutes}} min in total).
finding.maskOff_other: The mask was taken off {{count}} times (about {{minutes}} min in total).
finding.periodic: Periodic breathing was detected for about {{minutes}} min.
finding.reraHigh: The RERA index was {{index}} per hour.
finding.settingsChanged_one: {{count}} therapy setting changed on this night.
finding.settingsChanged_other: {{count}} therapy settings changed on this night.
finding.flatHigh: Flat-topped breaths were {{share}} % of breaths, above your usual {{usual}} %.
finding.periodicPattern: A waxing-and-waning breathing pattern was seen in about {{percent}} % of the night.
finding.desatFrequent: The oximeter recorded {{odi}} desaturations of 3 points or more per hour.
finding.lowOxygenTime: SpO₂ was under 90 % for {{percent}} % of the recording.
finding.oxygenSteady: The oximeter showed steady oxygen levels (lowest {{min}} %).

changes.title: Setting changes
changes.hint: Nights on which a therapy setting differs from the night before. Markers on the trend charts show the same dates.

equipment.title: Equipment
equipment.intro: Track your mask, cushion, hose and filter: how old each is, when to replace it, and whether leak rises as it ages.
equipment.hint: Replacement intervals are editable starting points. Follow your manufacturer's or clinician's guidance.
equipment.name: Name or model
equipment.none: No equipment yet. Add your mask to start tracking.
equipment.replaceConfirm: Mark {{name}} as replaced as of {{date}} and start a new one?
equipment.leakNeedMore: Not enough nights with leak data yet (at least 6 are needed).
equipment.trendRising: Leak is rising by about {{value}} L/min per 30 days of use.
equipment.trendFalling: Leak is falling by about {{value}} L/min per 30 days of use.
equipment.trendFlat: Leak is stable over the life of this item.
equipment.trendNote: A rise with age can have other causes too (fit, position, weight change, season).
equipment.asOf: Ages are counted up to your latest data ({{date}}).

compare.title: Compare periods
compare.intro: See what changed between two periods: before and after a new mask or a setting change, or this month against last month.
compare.presetChangeNone: No setting changes to compare around
compare.reportFor: Open a report for period B
compare.noData: One of the periods has no nights with data.
compare.settingsHint: Settings of the first night of each period.
compare.caution: A difference between periods is not proof that a change caused it: sleep, illness, season and mask fit also vary. Discuss results with your clinician.

report.title: Therapy report
report.intro: A printable summary for your clinician. Choose what to include, then print or save it as a PDF.
report.patientHint: Printed on the report only; never stored outside this browser.
report.includeNights: Include the table of every night
report.printHint: In the print dialog choose “Save as PDF”.
report.noData: There is no data in this period.
report.nightsWithData: Nights with data: {{count}} of {{total}} in the period
report.eventsHint: Rate per hour of use over the whole period.
report.noChanges: No setting changes in the period.
report.noPrevious: No data in the previous period.
report.limits: Figures come from the device's own records. Leak is the device's own figure: total leak including the mask's intentional vent flow for Philips, unintentional leak for ResMed. This summary is not a diagnosis.
report.refHint: Dashed horizontal lines mark 4 hours of use and 5 events per hour.
report.oximetryLine: {{count}} night(s) with data: average SpO₂ {{mean}} %, lowest {{min}} %, time under 90 % {{t90}} % (median), desaturations ≥ 3 % {{odi}} per hour (mean).
report.breathingLine: {{count}} night(s) with detailed flow: breath rate {{rate}} per minute (median), flat-topped breaths {{flat}} % (median), variation of breath length {{cv}} %.

breathing.title: Breathing (experimental)
breathing.note: Measured from the device's 5 Hz flow, so these are coarse trends inside your own data. They are not a diagnosis and cannot be compared with 25 Hz tools such as AirwayLab.
breathing.none: Breathing analysis needs the detailed flow data, which the card keeps only for recent nights.

anomaly.missedNights: {{missed}} of the last {{days}} nights have no data.
anomaly.shortRun: The last {{nights}} nights were all under 4 h.
anomaly.leakRise: Leak (95 %) over the last 3 nights ({{now}} L/min) is well above your usual {{usual}} L/min.
anomaly.ahiRise: Your AHI over the last 7 nights ({{now}} per hour) is about double your usual ({{usual}} per hour).
anomaly.note: These prompts compare you with your own recent history. They are not a diagnosis; if you are worried, talk to your clinician.

export.title: Export this night
export.hint: Times are the device's clock without a time zone. Flow is exported with the device's own numbers: ResMed flow is in L/min, for Philips the unit is not verified.

oximetry.title: Oximeter
oximetry.importIntro: If you also sleep with a pulse oximeter (for example a Wellue/Viatom ring), import its CSV export to see oxygen and pulse next to your therapy. The CPAP itself records no oxygen data.
oximetry.skipped: {{count}} rows could not be read and were ignored.
oximetry.dateOrder: The date order is ambiguous (03/04/2026). Read dates as month/day.
oximetry.offsetHint: If the oximeter's clock differs from the CPAP's, enter the minutes to add (negative to subtract).
oximetry.noOverlap: No overlap with your CPAP nights: check the clock correction.
oximetry.lowOverlap: Less than three quarters of your CPAP night is covered by this recording: check the dates and the clock correction.
oximetry.tooLarge: The file is larger than 50 MB.
oximetry.note: Recorded by your own oximeter, not by the CPAP. Clocks are compared as written; use the clock correction at import if they differ.

share.title: Share a snapshot
share.intro: Creates a link that contains the figures of this report. Whoever opens it sees the same summary, without needing the app's data. Nothing is uploaded: the data travels inside the link itself.
share.passphraseHint: With a passphrase the link is encrypted; give the passphrase to the recipient through a different channel.
share.warnPlain: Anyone who gets this link can read these figures. Treat it like the report itself.
share.warnEncrypted: The link is encrypted. The recipient needs the passphrase; if you forget it, create a new link.
share.tooLong: This link is {{chars}} characters long; some chat apps and email clients cut long links. Choose a shorter period.
share.contents: The link contains the nightly figures, the previous period if comparison is on, and setting changes. It never contains notes, equipment or the device serial number.
share.includesName: It also contains the name typed above.

shared.title: Shared snapshot
shared.intro: Someone shared a summary of their CPAP data with you.
shared.banner: Read-only snapshot created on {{date}}. It is not stored on this device and only contains what its sender chose to share. It is not a diagnosis.
shared.err_bad-link: This link is damaged or incomplete. Ask for a new one.
shared.err_wrong-passphrase: Wrong passphrase, or the link was changed.
shared.err_unsupported-version: This link was made by a newer version of the app. Update the app and try again.

llm.title: Written summary (experimental)
llm.introLocal: A short description of your last 30 days, written by the model "{{model}}" running on your own computer.
llm.introRemote: A short description of your last 30 days, written by a model on {{endpoint}}. The figures in the request leave this computer.
llm.disclaimer: Written by a language model from aggregate figures only. It can be wrong and is not a diagnosis or advice; talk to your clinician about your data.
llm.err_blocked: The summary is not allowed with the current settings.
llm.err_unreachable: Could not reach the model at {{endpoint}}. Is the server running and does it allow requests from this page?
llm.err_http: The model server returned an error. Check that the model name exists.
llm.settingsTitle: Written summary with a language model
llm.settingsIntro: Optional and off by default. Connects to a model you run yourself (an Ollama-compatible server) and asks it to describe your numbers in a few sentences.
llm.remoteWarning: This address is not on this computer. Your aggregate therapy figures would be sent to it.
llm.allowRemote: I understand and allow sending the figures to this server
llm.whatIsSent: Only totals for the last two 30-day periods are sent: nights of use, average hours, AHI, event rates, leak and setting changes. Never notes, names, serial numbers or individual nights.

reference.label: Reference
reference.usage: Reference: at least {{hours}} h per night
reference.compliance: Reference: at least {{hours}} h on {{share}} % of nights
reference.leak: Reference (ResMed): 70th percentile of the night under {{limit}} L/min
reference.leakPhilips: Philips total leak (vent flow included). Working reference: 30 to 50 L/min within range, above 60 L/min out of range; not yet sourced.
reference.odi4: Reference: under {{normal}} per hour (adult sleep-lab bands)
reference.none: No verified reference for this metric
reference.oximetryNote: The ODI bands come from sleep-lab (polysomnography) data. A home oximeter can give different values.
reference.footnote: References are orientative reading aids, not targets, and do not replace your clinician's judgement. The sources are being confirmed.
